teaser.text: 3i is an investment company: it buys and manages stakes in businesses, then earns from the value and cash those stakes produce. To understand its business, follow the money from a shopper or infrastructure user to the operating company, and from there—sometimes—to 3i.

blocks.heading: Where could 3i’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is 2,551.49p in October 2027, a 10% return including dividends. By October 2029, it is 3,295.66p, a 48% return including dividends. The forecast assigns 30% to the bear case and 50% to the base case. The bull case gets 20%.

The weighted price reaches 2887.67 in October 2028, equivalent to a 28% return. But the range remains wide: by October 2029, the bear case is 1925.54 and the bull case is 4842.46, compared with today’s 2406.00.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for 3i?

paragraphs.text: NAV is the main engine. The forecast starts from an estimated current book value of about £31,150m, based on post-dividend NAV and the reduced share count. The base case grows NAV to £43,515m by October 2029, using the company’s 15% annual total-return target as its planning anchor. The bear case reaches only £32,780m because slower Action growth and weaker marks absorb much of that return. The bull case reaches £49,779m because Action sustains earnings growth and exits support carrying values.

blocks.heading: How much cash does 3i really make?

paragraphs.text: The conventional bridge also looks healthy. Cash from operations was £998 million. After capital spending, lease payments and interest, free cash flow was £926 million. After treating stock awards as an economic cost to shareholders, “real” free cash flow was £914 million. But operating cash flow included £68 million of investment purchases and £853 million of investment proceeds, dividends and transfers between investment subsidiaries. It is real cash, but not pure cash from running businesses.

paragraphs.text: NAV estimates what each share represents after adding the value of investments and other assets and deducting liabilities. It resembles valuing a house, subtracting its mortgage and dividing the remaining equity among the owners. 3i reported NAV of 3,131p at June 2026; after its 48p dividend, the comparable figure was 3,083p. blocks.heading: How much does 3i pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The 4.5x trailing P/E is a poor guide; the 3.5% dividend yield is more directly tied to cash paid. Revaluations can dominate reported revenue, operating margin and EPS. 3i’s real free cash flow was 16.6% of revenue in FY2026, while net debt was £576 million. Real free cash flow per share rose from 42.22p in FY2022 to 92.99p in FY2026. Dividends paid per share rose from 40.16p to 77.83p.

paragraphs.text: Across the five years to March 2026, dividends dominated shareholder payments, alongside smaller share buybacks. Coverage varied sharply by year, so one year’s payout cannot establish a permanent policy. 3i says dividends should be maintained or grown, subject to a conservative balance sheet; that condition matters because investment proceeds arrive unevenly.

Dividends rise from £0.90 to £1.02 per share in the base case. That is slower than recent growth, but consistent with five consecutive increases and management’s aim to maintain or grow the dividend. The bear case falls to £0.68 as weaker cash generation causes cuts. The bull case reaches £1.23 because strong Action cash generation permits faster increases, although Action’s reinvestment and lender needs constrain distributions.

blocks.heading: What has 3i guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: 3i’s annual total-return target is 15%. Total return measures how much shareholders’ funds grow, including changes in the estimated value of businesses that 3i has not sold. It is not a promise to pay shareholders 15% in cash: a house that rises from £100 to £115 while paying £2 in rent has produced value growth, but only £2 has arrived as cash. The separate 8%–10% target belongs to 3i Infrastructure, not the whole Group.

Action, 3i’s largest portfolio company, plans at least 400 new stores during calendar 2026 and three new distribution centres. A shop can sell only what the logistics network can replenish, so the chain runs from buying goods to storing, transporting and selling them. Warehouses are therefore part of the sales engine, not background infrastructure.

ten23 health, which fills and finishes injectable medicines for pharmaceutical customers, expects two commercial-scale production lines in Visp to operate in 2027. 3i also plans a share buyback of up to £750 million by 31 December 2026. That reduces the number of shares sharing future value, but uses cash immediately.

paragraphs.text: His authority is supported by a measurable turnaround. In June 2012, he promised to simplify 3i and cut annual operating costs by more than £40 million. By March 2013, the annualised reduction had reached £51 million. “Annualised” means the saving expected over a full year at the new spending rate. The result helps explain the board’s continued support.

paragraphs.text: On 12 November 2026, 3i is scheduled to report its six-month results. Like-for-like sales measure growth in comparable shops, so they help separate stronger customer demand from sales created simply by opening more locations. Investors should read them alongside margins: higher sales matter less if labour, freight or discounting absorbs the gain.
